items.title: 19.1.2 Chemical Composition and Organization of Chromosome

source_refs.note: Topic 19.1.2 with the Tidbit (PDF 117-118); Figures 19.3 and 19.4 are replaced by the original diagram.

blocks.text: A chromosome is made of about 40% DNA and 60% protein (histones), and both chromatids have identical DNA molecules. The DNA in an average human chromosome is about 5 cm long and has about 140 million nucleotides. DNA is negatively charged because of its phosphate groups, and it binds strongly to histones, which are positively charged because they are rich in basic amino acids such as arginine and lysine.

items: Nucleosome string (11 nm): after replication about every 146 nucleotides of DNA (2 nm thick) wrap twice round a histone octamer, two copies each of H2A, H2B, H3 and H4, forming nucleosomes linked by about 80 nucleotides of linker DNA. The fifth histone, H1 (linker histone), sits at the base of the nucleosome where DNA enters and leaves and helps wind the chain. The nucleosomes look like beads on a string.
Chromatin fibre (30 nm): in the early stages of cell division the nucleosome string coils about its axis, and tightly packed nucleosomes make a thicker chromatin fibre.
Chromatids: the chromatin fibre folds on itself into a supercoil (300 nm), which coils and condenses further into a chromatid (700 nm).

blocks.alt: Top: a histone octamer drawn as a disc in two layers, its top divided into four coloured histones H2B, H3, H4 and H2A. Plus a wavy DNA strand of about 146 nucleotides. A green arrow leads to a nucleosome string: DNA wound round three octamers like beads on a string, with the histone H1 at the base of a nucleosome.
blocks.caption: Figure 19.3: Nucleosome string (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 19.3).
blocks.long_description: Labels: H2B, H3, H4, H2A, Histone octamer, DNA (about 146 nucleotides), Nucleosome, H1, Nucleosome string.

blocks.alt: One continuous drawing from top to bottom: the DNA double helix (2 nm); the DNA wound round red histone octamers to make nucleosomes joined by linker DNA, with a yellow linker histone on each (11 nm); the nucleosomes packed into a chromatin fibre (30 nm); the fibre folded into loops, the supercoil (300 nm); the loops coiled tightly into condensed chromatin (700 nm); and finally the duplicated chromosome, one chromatid 700 nm wide and both chromatids together 1,400 nm.

blocks.title: Tidbit: two regions in chromatin
blocks.text: Inactive portions of chromatin produce dark bands and are called heterochromatin, while active portions are called euchromatin.
